audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] hands Levels 2-3 and First item to Shen and calls Level 6 'Skill', while whys[2], whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] in the same object say Aatrox out-brawls the low-damage tank at 3, overwhelms him at 4-5, still wins the lane fight at 6, and shreds him at first item. whys[6] says the late game 'evens' but win[6] reads Shen.
audit.why: Shen has no kill pressure in a solo lane and the packet chart reads Aatrox through First item, then even. At 51.1% over 2489 games the lane is Aatrox-favoured until Stand United starts deciding other lanes.
audit.corrected: Levels 2 evens to Skill; Levels 3 through First item to Aatrox; Two+ items to Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stand United and Shadow Dash are discussed with no cooldowns, so 'ping when his R is up' has nothing to count from.
audit.why: Stand United is 200/180/160 and Shadow Dash is 18/16/14/12/10. A 200s rank-1 global is the single most trackable timer in the matchup and the reason Shen's lane presence collapses right after he uses it.
audit.corrected: 200s Stand United and 18s Shadow Dash added to spikes[1], spikes[2] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge is described as 'the shield that blocks autos' — it is not a shield, it is a zone around the spirit blade that blocks attacks aimed at Shen or allies inside it. Ki Barrier, the actual shield, is never mentioned at all, and it refreshes every time he casts a spell.
audit.why: Riot's text: Spirit's Refuge — 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked'; Ki Barrier — 'After casting a spell, Shen gets a shield.' The distinction matters because your Q casts and the drain from Umbral Dash still land inside the refuge, but Ki Barrier eats the front of every trade you open, so opening on a Shen who has just cast is throwing your first swing into a shield.
audit.corrected: Refuge named as a blade zone that stops basic attacks only; Ki Barrier named as the per-cast shield to open around.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says Stand United is an interruptible channel.
audit.why: Riot flags Stand United as a channel: Shen shields the ally, then teleports 'soon after'. Hard CC during that window cancels it, and the third Darkin Blade swing's knockup is the interrupt Aatrox owns. Denying a Shen global is worth more than the lane kill.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[1].text that a landed third-Q knockup cancels the channel.

edits.before: Your window — Shen is a low-damage tank early. With Q pattern + W, brawl him down: W-pull, Q-sweetspot, E-drain. Bait his Spirit's Refuge (the shield that blocks autos) by not auto-attacking into it — throw your Q casts instead, since ability hits still land, then commit when it fades.
edits.after: Your window — Shen is a low-damage tank early. With Q pattern + W, brawl him down: chain, Q-sweetspot, E-drain. Spirit's Refuge is a zone round his blade that blocks basic attacks only — throw Darkin Blade casts through it, drain off Umbral Dash, and auto once it fades.

edits.before: Shen's R (Stand United) is a global — the danger is him ulting to a fight elsewhere, not his lane combat. In lane your all-in still wins: R to out-sustain, drain through his chip, and force him to either die or waste his ult defensively. Ping when his R is up so your team plays around the global.
edits.after: Stand United is a 200s global — the danger is him joining a fight elsewhere, not lane combat. It is also a channel: land the third-Q knockup on him mid-cast and the whole thing is cancelled. Otherwise force him to die or burn it defensively, and ping the timer for your team.

edits.before: Eclipse/Profane lets you shred him through his tankiness. Shen has no kill pressure solo, so keep punishing — but watch for his taunt (E dash) pulling you into his jungler.
edits.after: Eclipse/Profane lets you shred him through his tankiness. Shen has no kill pressure solo, so keep punishing — but Shadow Dash is up every 18s and taunts you into his jungler.

edits.before: From level 3 you dominate — Shen is a low-damage tank and your combo plus drain out-brawl him easily. W-pull him, land the Q sweetspot, and E-drain, but don't auto into his Spirit's Refuge (it blocks basic attacks); throw your Q casts instead since ability damage still lands, then auto once it drops. At 6 his R is a global, so the lane danger is him ulting away — force him to either die to your all-in or burn his ult on defense. Ping when Stand United is up so your team respects the global.
edits.after: From level 3 you dominate — Shen is a low-damage tank and your combo plus drain out-brawl him. Chain him, land the third-Q knockup, E-drain, but never auto into Spirit's Refuge: that zone round his blade blocks basic attacks, not Darkin Blade casts, so cast through it and auto once it drops. Ki Barrier re-shields him after every spell, so open your trade on a Shen who has just cast. At 6, force him either to die to your all-in or to burn the 200s Stand United on defence.

edits.before: Farm safely and use taunt (E) to enable ganks
edits.after: Shadow Dash taunts you into a jungle collapse

edits.before: Shen changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Shen Q blade, E taunt, W, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Shen wants to survive lane, farm safely, stack durability, and become more valuable in later fights than the early lane suggests.
edits.after: Shen changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Spirit's Refuge blocking every basic attack aimed into it and Shadow Dash taunting him on an 18s cooldown. Aatrox wins by casting Darkin Blade through the refuge instead of auto-attacking into it, holding Umbral Dash for the taunt, and pinning Shen in lane so he never spends a 200s Stand United where it decides another fight.

edits.before: Shen Q blade, E taunt, W, and R

notes: champ-data/_kits/_missing/aatrox.json claims 'Shen's Stand United (R) is a channel — your World Ender (R) cancels it outright.' That is wrong and I did not write it: World Ender's hardCC flag comes from fearing nearby MINIONS, per Riot's own text, and it applies no crowd control to champions. The interrupt Aatrox actually has is the third Darkin Blade knockup, which is what I wrote instead. The generator rule that produced that headline will be producing the same false claim for every Aatrox-vs-channel matchup and should be reviewed.
